newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen $0.50 per cwt lower as sluggish pork demand continued to weaken cash pork prices and erode packer operating margins, dealers said.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $50.50 to $51.50 per cwt.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $50.50 to $51.00. Indidana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant door could range up to $51.00.
Hog movement on Monday was light, but enough to fill packer needs, the dealers said.
A few pork plants were closed in observance of Presidents Day holiday.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts were pegged at 100,000 head, compared with 100,000 a week ago and 103,000 a year ago, USDA said.
Fresh loins were steady in a light test at midday, hams were steady to $2.00 per cwt lower and pork bellies were $1.00 to $2.00 lower, USDA statistics showed. There were 33.5 pork loads sold.
